verdict.rationale: Phoenix documents an official remote MCP server at the instance's `/mcp` endpoint. Clients such as Claude Code, Cursor, and VS Code can use it to search, query, and operate on projects, traces, datasets, experiments, and annotations, which covers traces and eval results, and `px setup mcp` wires it into agents. The SDK also offers programmatic span querying with filtering. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of querying aggregate metrics (latency or token usage) through the MCP/API, and independent hands-on corroboration of agent-driven debugging via the MCP server.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can have an agent query my traces, metrics, and eval results through an API or MCP server to debug my app

citations.quote: Point any MCP-compatible client (Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, and others) at your Phoenix instance’s `/mcp` endpoint and it can search, query, and operate on your projects, traces, datasets, experiments, prompts, and annotations
Connect Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, or any MCP client to your live Phoenix data.
px setup mcp --agent claude   # or codex, gemini, cursor, opencode, vscode
Spans — Query and analyze traces with powerful filtering capabilities
